The 2026 United States House of Representatives election in Wyoming is scheduled to be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the U.S. representative for Wyoming's at-large congressional district. The election will coincide with other elections to the House of Representatives, elections to the United States Senate, and various state and local elections. The primary elections happened on August 18, 2026.[1]

Republican primary

[edit | edit source]

Candidates

[edit | edit source]

Nominee

[edit | edit source]
  • Chuck Gray, Wyoming Secretary of State (2023–present) and candidate for this seat in 2022[2]

Eliminated in primary

[edit | edit source]
  • Jillian Balow, former Virginia Superintendent of Public Instruction (2022–2023) and Wyoming Superintendent of Public Instruction (2015–2022)[3]
  • Bo Biteman, president of the Wyoming Senate (2025–present) from the 21st district (2019–present)[4]
  • Kevin Christensen, military veteran[5]
  • Richard Dodson, military veteran, entrepreneur[6]
  • Steve Friess, conservative activist and son of Foster Friess[7]
  • David Giralt, policy advisor to U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis[8]
  • Keith Goodenough, former Democratic state senator (1995–2005), former Casper city councilor (2006–2014), and candidate for U.S. Senate in 2008[6]
  • Reid Rasner, businessman and candidate for U.S. Senate in 2024[9]
  • John Romero-Martinez, former state representative from the 44th district (2021–2023)[10]

Withdrawn

[edit | edit source]
  • Frank Chapman, entrepreneur, rancher (remained on ballot)[11][12]

Declined

[edit | edit source]
  • Harriet Hageman, incumbent U.S. representative (running for U.S. Senate)[13]
  • Chip Neiman, speaker of the Wyoming House of Representatives (2025–present) from the 1st district (2021–present) (ran for state senate, endorsed Gray)[14][15]
